Parameters for adduct and fragment annotation

Source: R/AllClasses.R, R/methods-show.R
AdductVoteParam.Rd

AdductVoteParam() creates the parameter object for annotateAdducts().

Usage

AdductVoteParam(
  rules = NULL,
  ppm = 10,
  mzabs = 0.005,
  polarity = c("positive", "negative"),
  subset = integer(),
  value = "into",
  nBest = 3
)

# S4 method for class 'AdductVoteParam'
show(object)

Arguments

rules

data.frame with the adduct and fragment rules in CAMERA's format, with columns name, nmol, charge, massdiff, quasi and ips. NULL (the default) uses defaultAdductRules() for polarity.

ppm

numeric(1) relative tolerance (in ppm) for two neutral masses to be considered equal.

mzabs

numeric(1) absolute tolerance added to ppm.

polarity

character(1), "positive" or "negative". Selects the default rules.

subset

integer with the indices of the samples used to compute the representative intensity of each feature. An empty vector (the default) uses all samples. Only used by the XcmsExperiment method.

value

character(1) the type of feature value used for the intensities, see xcms::featureValues(). Only used by the XcmsExperiment method.

nBest

numeric(1) how many hypotheses per feature are written to the adduct text column. Inf writes all of them. All hypotheses are stored regardless; see adductHints() and formatAdducts().

object

an AdductVoteParam object.

Value

An AdductVoteParam object.

Details

Within each feature group, every feature is tried as every quasi-molecular ion of the rule list (rules with quasi == 1, such as [M+H]+). The neutral mass this implies is a hypothesis if at least one other feature of the group is explained by some rule as an ion of the same neutral mass. All hypotheses are kept and ranked by the summed rule score (ips) and then by the summed intensity of the features they explain.

See also

annotateAdducts(), defaultAdductRules(), IsotopologueParam()

Examples

AdductVoteParam()
#> Object of class "AdductVoteParam"
#>  rules: 159 rules, 5 quasi-molecular
#>  ppm: 10 
#>  mzabs: 0.005 
#>  polarity: positive 
#>  value: into 
#>  subset: all samples 
#>  nBest: 3 
AdductVoteParam(polarity = "negative", nBest = Inf)
#> Object of class "AdductVoteParam"
#>  rules: 147 rules, 5 quasi-molecular
#>  ppm: 10 
#>  mzabs: 0.005 
#>  polarity: negative 
#>  value: into 
#>  subset: all samples 
#>  nBest: Inf
